questions.stem: About the definitions of anatomy given in the course:
options: The word comes from Greek and Latin terms meaning "dissection" ("to cut through")
Rouvière defined it as the "science of body structures"
Paturet (1951) defined it as the "science whose object is the study of the constitution of organized beings"
Vesalius (1543) considered it "the only solid basis of the whole art of medicine"
Ribet (1961) defined it as the study of the external forms of the human body intended for artists
questions.explanation: Anatomy comes from the Greek anatomia / Latin anatomia = dissection. Ribet's definition is the study of the form, reciprocal relationships and final structure of organs; the study of external forms for artists is artistic anatomy.

options: The first anatomical descriptions on papyrus date back to 3000 BC
Hippocrates taught human anatomy in Greece
Aristotle used the term "anatomy" for the first time
Aristotle is the founder of pathological anatomy
Galen, "prince of physicians", carried out his research on human corpses
questions.explanation: Aristotle is the founder of comparative anatomy (pathological anatomy was founded by Morgagni in the 18th century). Galen conducted his research on monkeys, not on human corpses.

options: Ibn Sina (Avicenna) used corpses from the battlefields to dissect
Ibn an-Nafis gave the first description of the pulmonary circulation
Ibn Rushd (Averroes) wrote the "Canon of Medicine"
Ibn Al-Haitham was the first to describe the anatomy of the eye
Ibn Rushd (Averroes) wrote "Anatomy of the Organs"
questions.explanation: The "Canon of Medicine" was written by Ibn Sina; Ibn Rushd wrote "Anatomy of the Organs".

questions.stem: Which scientist gave the first description of the pulmonary circulation and wrote "Comments on the anatomy of the Canon of Ibn Sina"?
options: Ibn Rushd
Ibn Sina
Ibn an-Nafis
Ibn Al-Haitham
William Harvey
questions.explanation: Ibn an-Nafis (1213–1288) first described the pulmonary circulation. William Harvey, in the 17th century, only rediscovered and demonstrated it.

options: It covers the 15th and 16th centuries
Vesalius published "De Humani Corporis Fabrica" in 1543
Vesalius performed the first public dissection
Gabriel Fallopius described the uterine tube and the facial nerve
Jacques Dubois (Sylvius) gave the first description of the pulmonary circulation
questions.explanation: Renaissance anatomy spans the 15th–16th centuries; Vesalius wrote the Fabrica (1543) and performed the first public dissection. Sylvius described the middle cerebral artery; pulmonary circulation was first described by Ibn an-Nafis.

questions.stem: About the history of anatomy from the 17th to the 19th century:
options: William Harvey discovered the capillary vessels
Morgagni founded pathological anatomy
Aselli and Pecquet discovered and demonstrated the lymphatic circulation
Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895
Formaldehyde has been used as a fixative since around 1890
questions.explanation: The capillary vessels were discovered by Malpighi; Harvey rediscovered and demonstrated the pulmonary circulation.

options: The Visible Man Project (1993) is a 3D virtual man showing real human anatomy
The Visible Man was obtained after the dissection of a condemned man into 1800 thin slices
Topographic and surgical anatomy developed in the 20th century for the safety of amputations
Comparative anatomy was born in the 19th century
Cell theory was demonstrated in the 17th century
questions.explanation: Topographic and surgical anatomy developed in the 19th century (safety of amputations), the same period in which cell theory was demonstrated; comparative anatomy was born in the 18th century.

questions.stem: A student studies an isolated kidney: its shape, dimensions, weight, colour, consistency and internal structure. Which branch of anatomy is this?
options: Topographic anatomy
Descriptive anatomy
Functional anatomy
Artistic anatomy
Systemic anatomy
questions.explanation: Descriptive (explanatory) anatomy is the analytical study of the morphology of separate organs; it is the basic study in anatomy. Topographic anatomy would study the kidney's location and relations within its region.

options: Is also called functional anatomy
Studies the location and relationships of organs within the same anatomical region
Is the basic study of surgery
Is the basic study in anatomy
Studies the function of organs and its relationship to morphology
questions.explanation: Topographic (regional) anatomy studies location and relations of organs in one region and is the basis of surgery. The basic study in anatomy is descriptive anatomy; function vs morphology is functional anatomy.

questions.stem: Match each branch of anatomy with its definition:
options: Anthropological anatomy studies morphological variations in human races
Comparative anatomy studies homologous structures between individuals (ontogeny) or between species (phylogeny)
Radiological anatomy studies morphology using imaging techniques (X-ray, CT scan, MRI, scintigraphy)
Pathological anatomy studies the external forms of the human body
Systemic anatomy is anatomy applied to the clinic
questions.explanation: Pathological anatomy studies alterations of structures caused by diseases (external forms = artistic anatomy). Systemic anatomy studies the body's systems; anatomy applied to the clinic is medical-surgical (clinical, applied) anatomy.

options: Studies morphological transformations from fertilization to adulthood
Includes embryology
Includes fetology
Includes postnatal growth
Includes teratology (congenital malformations)
questions.explanation: Developmental anatomy covers prenatal development (embryology, fetology), postnatal development (growth) and teratology, from fertilization to adulthood.

questions.stem: Which branch of anatomy studies the external forms of the human body and is intended for sculptors, engravers and painters?
options: Anthropological anatomy
Artistic (plastic) anatomy
Descriptive anatomy
Comparative anatomy
Microscopic anatomy
questions.explanation: Artistic, plastic anatomy or anatomy of forms studies the external forms of the body for artists. Anthropological anatomy studies variations between human races.

options: Studies the structure of cells (cytology)
Studies the structure of tissues (histology)
Studies alterations of anatomical structures caused by diseases
Is the basic study of surgery
Uses endoscopy as its main method
questions.explanation: Microscopic anatomy is the microscopic study of cells (cytology) and tissues (histology). Disease-caused alterations are pathological anatomy; the basis of surgery is topographic anatomy.

questions.stem: Which of the following are study methods of anatomy listed in the course?
options: Dissection
Plastination
Endoscopy (bronchoscopy, rectoscopy)
Microscopy
Mummification
questions.explanation: The study methods are dissection, plastination, imaging, endoscopy, surgery and microscopy. Mummification is only cited as evidence of anatomical knowledge in antiquity.
